dedupe_keys.name: zhengzhou erqi district emergency response capacity of public services under pluvial flood scenarios

description: This case study proposes and applies a method to map the emergency response capacity of urban public services under different rainfall flooding scenarios in Erqi District, Zhengzhou, China. The authors, researchers at Henan Polytechnic University, simulated inundation area and depth with the SCS curve number runoff method for several rainfall return periods, computed spatial densities of inundation, road network and emergency public service institutions such as hospitals and fire stations, weighted the indicators with entropy and coefficient-of-variation methods, and combined them into a pixel-level capacity index. It is published in an open-access journal article. Coverage is one urban district at raster resolution. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the flood model is simplified, the index is a weighted overlay, not a simulation of response operations, and results were not checked against a real event. The study found clear spatial differences in capacity, with high-capacity areas shrinking and low-capacity areas growing as the rainfall return period increases. Simulation uses: a screening method for locating gaps in emergency service coverage under flood scenarios. Related records: the Kenya 2024 floods healthcare accessibility study (case_study-kenya-2024-floods-healthcare-accessibility) assesses flood impacts on access to health facilities.
